title: The Alibi of the Fens
premise: Estate lawyer Vesper Delacroix is paid a fortune in advance to prove that a murder scheduled to happen at the Hollow Fen estate's anniversary dinner has not yet occurred — a will, dated thirty years ago, names a beneficiary who will only inherit if she dies before the dinner. As Vesper investigates, they discover the will's author is their own presumed-dead mother, and that Vesper's entire identity as an orphaned, self-made lawyer was engineered to keep them invisible from the fen families. Untangling alibis from 1994, Vesper finds the 'murder' is a ritual of confession the family performs every decade, and the beneficiary is Vesper themselves. At the anniversary dinner, Vesper refuses the inheritance, exposes the living matriarch who faked her death to test her heirs, and chooses the found family they built over the blood one that hid them.
about_author: Jude Villalobos is the pen name of a former probate clerk who spent a decade reading other people's last words and decided to start writing a few of their own. They live near the marshes they write about and insist the fens keep their secrets better than any lawyer could.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid Twice
chapters.summary: Vesper Delacroix's POV. A nervous stranger retains Vesper with double fees to prove a murder hasn't happened yet, leaving only a will dated 1994 and a key. Vesper, who never loses a case, accepts against instinct. Beat: uneasy curiosity masking a hunger to be needed.

chapters.title: A Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Vesper examines the document at their cluttered office, finding impossible notarization stamps and their own surname hidden in the witness line. Their assistant Marisol jokes it's a hoax, but Vesper's hands shake. Beat: the first crack in Vesper's belief that their past is a blank page.

chapters.title: Hollow Fen Rising
chapters.summary: Vesper travels to the fen estate, meeting the Aldersey family: matriarch Edith's portrait, heir Ambrose's hostility, and housekeeper Nell's warmth. Everyone insists Edith died thirty years ago. Beat: Vesper feels watched, an outsider reading a room that knows them.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner Tradition
chapters.summary: Nell, over tea, explains the decennial dinner where the family toasts Edith and reads a sealed letter. This year, the will's terms surface. Vesper realizes the dinner is six days away. Beat: ticking-clock dread wrapped in domestic ritual.

chapters.title: Alibi, 1994
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, digging into the night of Edith's supposed death. Three family members each claim to have been elsewhere, and each alibi is documented with suspicious perfection. Beat: the thrill of the hunt souring into the sense that the alibis were manufactured for someone to find.

chapters.title: Marisol's Question
chapters.summary: Back home, Marisol confronts Vesper: why does a case about strangers feel personal? Vesper deflects, but that night dreams of a woman singing in reeds. Beat: found-family theme surfaces — Marisol is the only person who ever asks about Vesper's inner life.

chapters.title: The Reeds Remember
chapters.summary: Vesper searches the fen at dawn and finds Edith's 'grave' empty, a marker over marsh water. Ambrose catches them and warns them off with genuine fear, not menace. Beat: dread deepens; the estate is a stage set for a performance Vesper can't see.

chapters.title: Ambrose Breaks
chapters.summary: Ambrose's POV. He recalls the 1994 dinner, his mother alive and laughing, and the pact the siblings swore to protect a secret. He nearly tells Vesper, then stops when his sister Camille appears. Beat: guilt as a family inheritance.

chapters.title: Camille's Ledger
chapters.summary: Vesper discovers Camille has kept meticulous records of every anniversary dinner — including one entry naming a 'visitor from the city' who came in 2004. The description matches a younger Vesper. Beat: vertigo; Vesper's past is not blank but erased.

chapters.title: The Orphan File
chapters.summary: Vesper pulls their own adoption records, finding the lawyer who processed them was the same notary who stamped the impossible will. Their identity was legally constructed. Beat: identity crisis — who was Vesper before the paperwork?

chapters.title: Nell's Kitchen Confession
chapters.summary: Nell admits she recognized Vesper on day one: Vesper has Edith's eyes. She reveals Edith sent Vesper away as a child to protect them from a family crime. Beat: warmth and grief entwined; the found family theme sharpens against blood ties.

chapters.title: The Crime Beneath the Will
chapters.summary: Vesper reconstructs 1994: Edith's brother drowned in the fen, and the family covered it up; Edith's 'death' was her exile-by-choice, her will a time bomb to force confession. Beat: the murder to be proven hasn't happened — but one did, thirty years ago.

chapters.title: Camille's Countermove
chapters.summary: Camille offers Vesper money to leave before the dinner, revealing she knows exactly who Vesper is and fears the will's terms will destroy them. Vesper refuses. Beat: temptation and defiance; Vesper's pride as a case-closer becomes armor.

chapters.title: A Letter in Reeds
chapters.summary: Following Nell's hint, Vesper finds Edith's hidden letters — she is alive, living as a fen hermit, and has watched Vesper's whole life from a distance. Beat: heartbreak; being protected meant never being known.

chapters.title: The Meeting in the Marsh
chapters.summary: Vesper confronts Edith at her hut. Edith explains the will: the beneficiary who inherits if she 'dies' before the dinner is Vesper — the terms force the family to either confess the 1994 crime or lose the estate. Beat: anger, longing, and the question of whether love can be a legal instrument.

chapters.title: Marisol Arrives
chapters.summary: Worried, Marisol drives to the fen uninvited, planting herself in Vesper's investigation. Her practical loyalty steadies Vesper. Beat: found family made explicit — Vesper realizes they already have the belonging the Alderseys never gave.

chapters.title: The Eve of the Dinner
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. All evidence assembled, Vesper drafts two endings: one that exposes the family, one that protects them. Ambrose quietly asks which they'll choose. Beat: hushed tension before the storm; Vesper must decide what closing a case means.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: The family gathers; the sealed letter is read; the will's terms are invoked. Camille moves to declare Edith legally dead and seize control. Vesper stands and stops the reading. Beat: climax ignition — the ritual becomes a trial.

chapters.title: The Glass Raised
chapters.summary: Vesper presents the 1994 truth: the brother's drowning was an accident the family let Edith carry alone, and her 'murder' is the confession they owe. Edith enters the room, alive. Beat: climax — secrets detonate in candlelight; alibis unravel one by one.

chapters.title: What the Will Actually Wanted
chapters.summary: Edith reveals the will's final clause: she never wanted Vesper to inherit the estate, only to be acknowledged. Vesper declines the inheritance publicly, renouncing the blood claim. Beat: catharsis; identity reclaimed as chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: The Case Vesper Couldn't Close
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, days later. The Alderseys scatter into uneasy honesty; Edith chooses her hermitage; Ambrose writes to Vesper. Vesper closes the file unfinished and finds that acceptable for the first time. Beat: bittersweet resolution; perfection released.

chapters.title: The Alibi of the Fens
chapters.summary: Vesper and Marisol share tea in the office as a new client knocks. Vesper keeps one fen reed in a jar on the desk — proof they existed before the paperwork. Beat: quiet hope; found family affirmed, memory owned, identity chosen.
